Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ShapeClust 0.4.0

  • shape_mixture(): Gaussian mixture with a spherical variance per cluster (mclust model VII) in tangent PCA coordinates (same scores and K - 1 floor as shape_ensemble()), with its own EM (k-means++ multiple starts, variance floor, empty-component restarts, flagged k-means fallback), no new dependency. For clusters of unequal spread, where k-means and k-means ensembles misassign the tail of the diffuse cluster. Returns posteriors, means, variances, proportions, log-likelihood and real representatives.

  • shape_ensemble() gains base = c("kmeans", "vii"). The default keeps all earlier results identical; "vii" fits the mixture on each bootstrap resample and assigns all observations by maximum posterior.

  • shape_ensemble() and shape_attention() keep at least K - 1 principal components (before: at least 2). On 260 primate crania with K = 4 the 90% variance rule kept 2 components and split the largest species. Results with K <= 3 are unchanged.

  • shape_attention(): self-attention smoothing of shapes before clustering. Each configuration is replaced by a softmax-weighted average of the others in tangent (PCA) coordinates, with per-row temperatures set to a fixed perplexity, as a transformer layer with no trained projections; layers can be stacked (blurring mean shift) and a residual weight keeps part of each point. The smoothed points are clustered by k-means or PAM. Reports the share of attention inside each point’s cluster as a diagnostic. Experimental: in simulations it helped only with many landmarks and moderate sample sizes.

  • shape_ensemble(): consensus clustering of landmark arrays. Bootstrap k-means in tangent PCA coordinates (90% variance rule, 2 to 10 components), co-association matrix, spectral partition, and the real observation closest to each cluster’s Procrustes mean as representative. Reproduces the reference implementation used in the authors’ 3D simulation study for the same RNG state.

  • hopkins_shape(): Hopkins test of clustering tendency for 2D/3D landmark arrays with a Monte Carlo p-value (tangent Gaussian or uniform null).

  • shape_pam() and shape_rankkmed() accept a real k x m x n landmark array (distances from shape_distance()). 2D inputs give the same results as before.

  • New vignette shapes-3d: simulation, clustering, bagging, hopkins_shape() and the macaque skulls of ‘shapes’.

3D shapes

The package now clusters configurations of landmarks in two or three dimensions given as real k x m x n arrays. The complex 2D interface (landmarks_to_preshape(), rho_matrix(), dF_matrix(), shape_pam(), shape_rankkmed()) is unchanged, and bagclust1() returns the same results as 0.3.0 for the same 2D calls (tested).

  • shape_distance(): Riemannian, full Procrustes and partial Procrustes distance matrices ("rho", "dF", "dP") in C++, from the singular values of the cross-product of Helmert pre-shapes. Reflections are kept unless reflection = TRUE. Agrees with shapes::riemdist() and shapes::procdist() (tested), and with rho_matrix() in 2D.
  • shape_mean(): full Procrustes mean (shapes::procGPA()) and MDS/phi mean (shapes::MDSshape()).
  • shape_kmeans(): Lloyd’s algorithm with a Procrustes or phi mean, a port of LloydShapes() and LloydShapes.phi() of the 3D bagging scripts.
  • shape_clarans(): FastCLARANS with R’s random-number stream, defaults numlocal = 2, maxneighbor = 0.0125 as in the scripts. No dependency on ‘fastkmedoids’. With these defaults no swap is tried when n - K <= 80 (see the help page).
  • shape_hill(): the hill-climbing search of the scripts, with the same random draws (tested against a transcription). As in the script every neighbor is a modification of the initial medoids; from_best = TRUE gives hill climbing in the usual sense.
  • bagclust1() accepts a real landmark array as well as complex pre-shapes, base = "kmeans", "clarans" and "hill", distance = "dP" and, for real arrays, reflection. For "kmeans" every replicate labels all observations by the nearest bootstrap center.
  • sim_shapes3d(): noisy cubes and parallelepipeds (8 or 34 landmarks, isotropic or anisotropic), reproducing the generators of the scripts draw for draw, with no dependency on ‘mvtnorm’ or ‘CircStats’.
  • ‘mvtnorm’ added to Suggests (a test compares the simulator with mvtnorm::rmvt()).

ShapeClust 0.3.0

Portability and checks

  • Added src/Makevars and src/Makevars.win: complex matrix products in the C++ layer need BLAS at link time.
  • Added tests/testthat.R, so R CMD check runs the test suite.
  • bagclust1() now handles parallel::detectCores() returning NA and stops with the original message when a parallel replicate fails. The comparison of serial and parallel runs is now tested on Windows too.

Bug fixes (change numerical results)

  • shape_rankkmed() now follows Zadegan et al. (2013) as implemented in kmed::rankkmed(): hostility is computed over the m nearest objects of each medoid, and colliding medoids are relocated at random to objects outside every group. Previously the hostility was summed over the whole assigned cluster, where it is constant whenever the cluster consists of mutual nearest neighbours, so the update picked the lowest-indexed member; and no relocation step existed. Partitions now equal those of kmed::rankkmed() for the same distances and random stream (tested).
  • bagclust1() now lets every replicate label all n observations by their nearest bootstrap medoid, as in Dudoit and Fridlyand (2003). Previously only the in-bag observations (about 63%) voted in each replicate.
  • select_K(method = "gap") drew its null reference by permuting the rows and columns of the distance matrix, which leaves the clustering problem unchanged and made the gap close to zero for every K. The reference is now a uniform sample on the shape space, and K is chosen by the one-standard- error rule of Tibshirani et al. (2001). The gap needs pre-shapes, not distances.
  • riemannian_variances() now uses full Procrustes means (Kent 1994) instead of the sample medoid, and no longer claims to use ‘shapes’.

Other changes

  • bagclust1() draws one seed per replicate, so results are identical with and without parallel = TRUE.
  • Functions with a seed argument restore the caller’s random-number stream.
  • Removed the no-op arguments center (landmarks_to_preshape()) and verbose (shape_pam()).
  • Examples for every exported function; regression tests for each fix.

ShapeClust 0.2.0 (2026-07-12)

Major changes

  • Full pipeline rebuilt on top of Rcpp + RcppArmadillo. Hot paths (Riemannian distance matrix, PAM swap-cost, rank matrix, hostility update) are now O(k) per pair and BLAS-backed.
  • New bagclust1() function wrapping any base clusterer in the BagClust1 bootstrap ensemble of Dudoit & Fridlyand (2003), with Hungarian label alignment via clue::solve_LSAP when available.
  • New select_K() helper implementing silhouette width and gap statistic in shape space.
  • New sim_complex_bingham() using the Simplex-truncation generator of Kent et al. (2004).
  • Full unit-test suite (40 tests, testthat).
  • Package now passes R CMD check --as-cran with zero warnings and zero notes.

New functions

  • helmert_submatrix(), landmarks_to_preshape()
  • rho_matrix(), dF_matrix()
  • shape_pam(), shape_rankkmed()
  • bagclust1(), align_labels()
  • rand_index(), fmi_index(), relative_gain(), riemannian_variances(), wilcoxon_paired_gain()
  • sim_complex_bingham(), sim_landmark_gaussian()
  • select_K()

ShapeClust 0.1.0

  • Initial pure-R prototype.
